header:
Date: 2026-04-21
Time: 10:30 AM UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Kumar (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood Solutions), Evan Hart (Valence VP Partnerships), Maya Chen (Valence Head Cloud Partnerships), Carlos Ruiz (Valence Solutions Architect), Samira Patel (Valence Security)
summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood Inference and Valence Cloud. Discussed Valence's partner go-to-market, technical integration points (VPC peering, private deployments), GPU/instance types, and compliance needs. Agreed to schedule a technical deep-dive and exchange network diagrams and a partner deck. High-level interest in a reseller/managed offering with co-sell motion.
topics: Integration options (VPC, private control plane, on-prem connectors)
Performance and hardware mapping (A100/H100 equivalence, quantization)
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone thanks for hopping on, i'll kick us off, i'm jordan from redwood inference, ae on the west coast, with priya our se.
[00:07] Evan Hart: thanks jordan yeah evan here from valence, we wanted to learn more about how you think about partner integrations and private deployments.
[00:15] Priya Kumar: great, yeah quick agenda - intro, partner motions, technical touchpoints, next steps. does that work?
[00:21] Maya Chen: works for me, we have about 45 minutes.
[00:25] Liam O'Connor: i'll add - quick note on the things we usually surface: network, kms, and how you handle dedicated pools.
[00:33] Carlos Ruiz: and any latency/cost numbers versus the big clouds would be great.
[00:38] Jordan Lee: totally. high level - redwood provides hosted api, dedicated reserved capacity, and private/vpc options. customers usually start hosted then move to dedicated or private as they scale, but that could be reversed for regulated customers.
[00:53] Evan Hart: when you say private, is that like a private control plane in our vpc or fully on-prem?
[00:58] Priya Kumar: both - we have a private control plane where the control plane is shared but the compute lives in your VPC, and for air-gapped setups we have on-prem packages. some callers call it VPC-on-prem confusion in our docs sorry.
[01:13] Maya Chen: ok that sounds promising. our main go-to-market ask is: can we resell and manage customer onboarding under our brand?
[01:20] Jordan Lee: yes, we support reseller/partner contracts, co-sell motions, and white-label APIs in certain enterprise arrangements; typical path involves an initial POC, then a partner reseller agreement.
[01:31] Evan Hart: who typically owns the integration work - redwood se or the partner?
[01:35] Priya Kumar: usually we collaborate - partner does the cloud/network setup and we provide runbooks, se support, and a couple days of integration help. for bigger deals we do a split statement of work.
[01:47] Carlos Ruiz: on the infra side, can you map your instance types to common public GPU instances so we can size? we primarily use H100s in prod.
[01:55] Priya Kumar: yep, we maintain a performance catalog; for H100 equivalence we recommend our high-throughput profiles, but there are quantization profiles that let you land on lower memory cards depending on model and seq len. we'll send the catalog.
[02:09] Jordan Lee: quick commercial note - Dedicated is commonly committed monthly or annually, reserved capacity. Hosted is pay-as-you-go. partners can have partner pricing tiers that we can go over.
[02:20] Samira Patel: security - what are default encryption in transit and at rest?
[02:24] Priya Kumar: in transit we use TLS, and at rest we integrate with customer KMS for private deployments; for hosted we encrypt with our KMS and can do bring-your-own-key on higher tiers. audit logs are retained per contract.
[02:36] Samira Patel: do you have SOC2?
[02:38] Jordan Lee: yes, redwood is SOC2 type ii; we also have ISO in progress and can provide the package for partners.
[02:45] Evan Hart: great. on networking - VPC peering vs private link vs egress rules - what's easiest for partners?
[02:53] Priya Kumar: VPC peering is straightforward for many partners. we also support private link and customer managed NAT. for on-prem we have an edge connector. there can be slight mis-terms because some docs refer to "private control plane" and "private compute" differently, sorry for any confusion.
[03:10] Carlos Ruiz: latency targets? we run latency-sensitive inferencing, sub-300ms target for 8k-context LLMs.
[03:18] Priya Kumar: for hosted low-latency targets we can hit 100-300ms for typical 4k seq models depending on hardware; for very long context and high concurrency you might want dedicated pools. we can run benchmarks.
[03:31] Jordan Lee: would love to understand a typical customer you see - is it ISV, enterprise?
[03:36] Evan Hart: Valence is an MSP; we want to offer redwood as a managed inference option to our customers, co-branded, and provide hosting in our cloud regions (eu-west, us-east, ap-sg).
[03:50] Maya Chen: region support is important; some customers have strict EU data residency needs.
[03:55] Priya Kumar: we support region pinning for dedicated and private. hosted may have regions we run in, but dedicated/pvt you can choose.
[04:03] Carlos Ruiz: about model variants - do you do automatic fallbacks if capacity is constrained?
[04:08] Jordan Lee: yes our smart routing can fallback to compatible model variants, or route to a different region or lower-cost quantized profile. you can opt-in to graceful degradation policies.
[04:19] Evan Hart: pricing - do partners get margin or reseller discounts? how flexible are price bands?
[04:24] Jordan Lee: partners get a tiered discount model; margins depend on commitment. we'll put numbers in the spreadsheet.
[04:30] Maya Chen: any constraints on license or redistribution?
[04:33] Jordan Lee: standard partner agreement covers redistribution and resale; we can share templates. legal usually signs an MSA + partner addendum.
[04:40] Liam O'Connor: i'd like to highlight a couple of technical caveats - model cache sizing for streaming workloads and kv cache handling across nodes can drive memory needs.
[04:50] Priya Kumar: yes - for streaming chat you want a good KV cache hit-rate strategy; we can recommend batching config and cache TTLs.
[04:58] Carlos Ruiz: what about quantization - do you recommend int8 or int4 for H100? we've seen quality regressions.
[05:05] Priya Kumar: tradeoffs - int8 on many models gives significant cost savings with modest quality impact; int4 can be more aggressive and model-dependent. we provide quality monitoring and regressions alerts tied to eval prompt sets. we'll share suggested profiles.
[05:19] Evan Hart: are there existing partners already doing reseller work for you? any references?
[05:23] Jordan Lee: yes we have a few partners - happy to share a brief reference list, will redact customer names as needed.
[05:29] Maya Chen: on the legal/compliance track, our customers will ask for audit logs retention of 12 months and SSO integration via SAML.
[05:38] Samira Patel: and encryption key custody - BYOK is key for many of our enterprise customers.
[05:43] Priya Kumar: BYOK supported on private and higher-tier dedicated; we integrate with common cloud kms providers and HSM options for on-prem.
[05:51] Carlos Ruiz: what's the typical onboarding timeline for a partner-managed customer?
[05:55] Jordan Lee: POC to production typically 4-8 weeks for a small customer; larger enterprise with compliance can be 2-3 months. partner onboarding has a runbook and a partner success manager assigned.
[06:06] Evan Hart: interesting, for our go-to-market we want co-sell with lead referral and joint demo decks. is that something you facilitate?
[06:13] Jordan Lee: yes, we have co-sell enablement materials, joint marketing funds in some programs, and partner portal access.
[06:20] Maya Chen: technical question - how do upgrades and model rollouts work in private deployments?
[06:25] Priya Kumar: in private we can do in-place rollouts controlled by the customer; for VPC-hosted compute we coordinate canary then full rollback if regressions. we also support pinned versions.
[06:36] Carlos Ruiz: what telemetry do you expose? we need per-route latency, token counts, and request/response tracing.
[06:43] Priya Kumar: console exposes token-level cost, per-route latency histograms, traces, and error rates. there are API endpoints to pull metrics into your monitoring stack.
[06:52] Evan Hart: any gotchas we should be aware of for networking setup?
[06:56] Priya Kumar: NAT egress rules, port whitelisting for health checks, and ensuring your subnet has enough IPs for autoscaling are common items. also, if using private link we need specific service endpoints.
[07:09] Jordan Lee: maybe let's move to action items - we'll share a partner deck and the performance catalog. Priya - can you own the performance notes?
[07:18] Priya Kumar: sure i'll draft a note comparing H100/A100, recommended batch sizes, and quantization options.
[07:23] Carlos Ruiz: i'll send over network diagrams and region requirements.
[07:26] Samira Patel: i'll assemble compliance checklist and must-have controls.
[07:29] Evan Hart: i'll coordinate partner legal and loop in our commercial lead.
[07:33] Jordan Lee: perfect. do you want a technical deep dive next week? we were thinking wed 2026-04-28, same time?
[07:41] Maya Chen: wed works for us.
[07:43] Jordan Lee: great i'll send calendar invite. any other questions?
[07:47] Maya Chen: one small thing - do you allow partner-managed billing or centralized billing with chargebacks?
[07:52] Jordan Lee: both options supported - invoicing can be direct to customer, billed to partner with chargebacks, or via reseller arrangements. we'll include billing options in the deck.
[07:59] Carlos Ruiz: thanks everyone this was helpful.
[08:02] Jordan Lee: thanks all - we'll follow up with the materials and the invite.
[08:06] Evan Hart: thanks jordan, priya. bye.
[08:08] [call end]
notes: References made to runbooks, partner deck, performance catalog, and onboarding checklist. Mentioned possible POC and co-sell model. Security asks: SOC2, BYOK, SAML, audit logs retention. Technical asks: network diagram, region pinning, benchmarks for H100/A100, quantization profiles.
